minimum_floor_menuiserie_candidate.label: FIXEO_POLICY — not market fact
minimum_floor_menuiserie_candidate.rationale: Menuiserie minimum structurally higher than Bricolage (200 MAD) due to: specialist precision tools (drill, chisel, level, rabot), hardware diagnosis skill, hardware sourcing complexity, greater setup burden, higher qualification. Standard menuisier daily rate 300-500 MAD/day (lechantier.ma Grade B). At 30-min minimum visit: 150-250 MAD pure labour + 80-150 MAD burdened travel/tool overhead = 230-400 MAD effective cost floor. 300 MAD is the mid-point of the justified range.
minimum_floor_menuiserie_candidate.architecture: EMBEDDED_IN_SERVICE_PRICES — not a separate charge; see anti_double_charge_doctrine

anti_double_charge_doctrine.rule: FINAL_PRICE = max(MENUISERIE_MINIMUM, STANDARD_SERVICE_PRICE) — never minimum + service
anti_double_charge_doctrine.example_correct: If minimum = 300 MAD and door adjustment = 350 MAD → client pays 350 MAD
anti_double_charge_doctrine.example_wrong: 300 MAD minimum + 350 MAD adjustment = 650 MAD — PROHIBITED
anti_double_charge_doctrine.rationale: Minimum is a floor protecting the artisan on simple/quick work. It does not add to legitimate service prices that already exceed the floor.

part_supply_model.model_a: CLIENT_SUPPLIED_PART — acceptable when client provides compatible compatible part; artisan must verify compatibility before installation; no warranty on client-supplied hardware
part_supply_model.model_b: ARTISAN_SUPPLIED_AT_DISCLOSED_PRICE — artisan sources, discloses cost, client approves. Preferred: artisan efficiency, correct part guaranteed
part_supply_model.model_c: PART_INCLUDED_IN_FIXED_PRICE — REJECTED for variable hardware (hinge type, runner quality create 3× cost variation). Acceptable only for consumables (screws, wood glue) below 10 MAD total
part_supply_model.rationale_reject_c: Standard vs soft-close hinge: 20-40 MAD vs 59-120 MAD. Bundling at mid-price is either unfair to artisan (on soft-close job) or unfair to client (on standard job). Transparency requires disclosure.

hardware_sourcing_policy.scenario_a: Client already has compatible part → artisan installs → no sourcing charge
hardware_sourcing_policy.scenario_b: Artisan brings likely compatible standard part (hinge, basic runner) → install → disclose part cost
hardware_sourcing_policy.scenario_c: Artisan diagnoses need but must source non-standard/unavailable part → SEPARATE QUOTE for return visit
hardware_sourcing_policy.return_visit_policy: If artisan must leave, source, and return → treat as second intervention; price separately or as quoted package. Do not hide sourcing time in first-visit labour.
hardware_sourcing_policy.recommendation: Artisans should carry a basic toolkit of most common hinges (standard + soft-close) and runners (standard pair 35-40cm, 45cm, 50cm) to minimize return visits.

custom_fabrication_doctrine.rationale: Material choice alone (mélaminé vs MDF laqué vs bois massif) creates 3-5× price variation. Scope definitions (upper+lower vs lower only; worktop included or not; hardware brand) create further 30-50% variation. CuisinAffaires (25,000+ kitchens) explicitly states prix au mètre is misleading. No standardization possible without full client brief and site measurement.

batch_economics_analysis.question: Should 1 hinge and 4 hinges on the same cabinet have the same labour fee?
batch_economics_analysis.analysis: Replacing 1 hinge: dismantle door, remove old hinge, fit new hinge, rehang door, adjust — 20-30 min. Replacing 4 hinges on same door (or two doors same cabinet): door already off, 4× hinge swap — adds ~15-20 min. Replacing 4 hinges on 2 different cabinets: 2 doors-off cycles — adds ~30 min.

architecture_options.option: A — One-visit flat fee (up to 4 hinges)
architecture_options.assessment: Simple for client. Unfair to artisan on single-hinge job vs 4-hinge. But 20-30 MAD per additional hinge hardware limits artisan exposure. Acceptable if flat labour = value for 2-hinge average.
architecture_options.verdict: ACCEPTABLE if fee is set at 2-hinge equivalent (~250-300 MAD)

architecture_options.option: B — Base visit + incremental per extra hinge
architecture_options.assessment: More precise. Base: 250 MAD (covers visit + 1st hinge). Each additional hinge same door/visit: +50 MAD labour. Simple math for artisan. Transparent for client.
architecture_options.verdict: RECOMMENDED — avoids flat-fee distortion at extremes

architecture_options.assessment: 150 MAD per hinge seems reasonable but: 4 hinges = 600 MAD labour alone, which is 2× a full door install. Overprices batch. Underprices single visit (travel is fixed cost).
architecture_options.verdict: REJECTED — creates unreasonable totals at scale

batch_economics_analysis.recommended_architecture: Option B: base_visit (250 MAD labour, covers 1 hinge) + additional_hinge_same_visit (50 MAD labour each). Cap: same door only for incremental; different cabinet = new base visit.

candidate_prices_tested.assessment: 20% commission → artisan 200 MAD gross. Mid-travel 100 MAD → net 100 MAD for 30 min skilled work. Tight but at hard floor. Acceptable only with incremental model where 2nd-4th hinges add margin.
candidate_prices_tested.verdict: MINIMUM viable for base; needs incremental to work economically

candidate_prices_tested.assessment: 20% commission → artisan 240 MAD. Mid-travel → net 140 MAD. 30-45 min work. Comfortable.
candidate_prices_tested.verdict: RECOMMENDED BASE — with +50 MAD each extra hinge same visit

batch_economics_analysis.question: 2 drawers same cabinet — same or doubled labour?

batch_economics_analysis.recommendation: BASE visit (1 drawer) + INCREMENTAL per additional drawer same cabinet/same visit
